### 6. Problem tree (visible materials only)
- Root P0 = first installment (customer tool). Plan hub: "The first installment of a payment plan is not fixed until the eligibility-transition waiver owed on the late fee of the enrollment's most recent billing month has been worked out and posted." Records: Dec late fee 55.00, no credit on it. Write found in "Eligibility-Transition Waiver of Pre-K Tuition Late Fees" (Posting the waiver). **state-derived**.
- P1 waiver ← P2 reversal. Waiver hub: "The eligibility-transition waiver of a late fee is fixed only after the late-fee reversal owed for the month's eligibility credit has been worked out and posted." Write found in "Reversal of Pre-K Tuition Late Fees on Eligibility-Credited Months". **state-derived**. Also the waiver applies only "when the tuition charge … carries an eligibility credit" — currently none on record.
- P2 reversal ← P3 eligibility credit. Reversal hub: "The late-fee reversal is not fixed until the eligibility credit owed on the month's tuition has been worked out and posted." Records: basis (reduced-price, 12-17) on file, enrollment moved, no "eligibility established" credit on the Dec charge. Write found in "Tuition Credits When a Pre-K Child Becomes State-Eligible" ("The basis month itself … is credited under the basis-month schedule"). **state-derived**.
- P3 hub carries no prerequisite sentence. Order P3 → P2 → P1 → P0.
Counter-proofs: "just set up the plan" is excluded by the plan hub's sentence and by P3's rule that the basis month is credited; "credit December in full" excluded (the move takes effect on the first day of the billing month after the basis is on file; the basis month goes under the basis-month schedule); "credit Aug–Nov" excluded ("months before the basis month remain owed"); Ivy's tier counted for the extra-installment schedule excluded ("the meal status of a brother or sister does not count") but counted for household-size schedules ("Every active meal account of the household counts"); a waiver of 20.00 excluded by the Standing-Part Rule.
